    • Observed at 21:32:30 Eastern time ET
      Pay Tel Communications, Inc. v. FCC, et al (opens in a new tab)
      Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca1-24-01969 / USCOURTS-ca1-24-01969-0

      FAPD-AI: The First Circuit addressed jurisdictional questions in consolidated petitions for review of the Federal Communications Commission's July 2024 order establishing rate caps for incarcerated people's communications services under the Martha Wright-Reed Just and Reasonable Communications Act of 2022. The court declined to transfer the petitions to the Fifth Circuit and held them in abeyance pending potential new FCC action. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    • Observed at 21:32:30 Eastern time ET
      Pay Tel Communications, Inc. v. FCC, et al (opens in a new tab)
      Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca1-24-01969 / USCOURTS-ca1-24-01969-1

      FAPD-AI: The First Circuit ruled on consolidated petitions for review of the FCC's 2024 and 2025 orders regulating incarcerated people's communications services rates. The court dismissed petitions filed by service providers, dismissed portions of state governments' petitions for lack of jurisdiction or as moot, and placed portions of nonprofit organizations' petitions in abeyance pending further proceedings on the 2025 order. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 21:32:30 Eastern time ET
    United States v. Ronnie Gideon (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca8-25-03134 / USCOURTS-ca8-25-03134-0

    FAPD-AI: Ronnie Gideon appealed his sentences for receipt and distribution of child pornography imposed by the Western District of Missouri. The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the sentences, concluding the district court did not abuse its discretion in imposing below-Guidelines prison terms. The court also rejected various other challenges Gideon raised regarding sentencing conditions and electronic device return. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    United States v. James Hatten, II (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca8-25-03347 / USCOURTS-ca8-25-03347-0

    FAPD-AI: James L. Hatten appealed his sentence and restitution for sex offenses following his guilty plea under a plea agreement containing an appeal waiver.     Hill v. Rankins (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-06152 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-06152-0

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit denied Patrick Henry Hill's request for a certificate of appealability to appeal the district court's dismissal of his federal habeas corpus petition challenging his 2002 state court manslaughter conviction, holding that the petition was untimely filed under the one-year limitations period. The court determined that Hill's claim of actual innocence based on new medical evidence did not satisfy the standard for gateway relief because his knowing and voluntary guilty plea undermined the claim and his lack of awareness of alternative medical conclusions does not establish an unintelligent plea. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Massey v. Rithm Capital Corp., et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-01367 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-01367-0

    FAPD-AI: Massey appealed the district court's denial of his motion to remand a diversity jurisdiction case to state court and the dismissal of his civil action against Rithm Capital Corporation and Newrez LLC. The appellate court affirmed, finding complete diversity of citizenship existed among the parties under 28 U.S.C. § 1332 and that res judicata barred Massey's claims based on his prior litigation regarding a lost payoff check. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 18:25:12 Eastern time ET
    Dickerson v. Miller (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-05054 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-05054-0

    FAPD-AI: Dickerson sought habeas relief challenging his conviction for first-degree child abuse murder of his infant daughter, specifically arguing that his appellate counsel was ineffective for failing to raise a claim that trial counsel ineffectively conducted its investigation into potential natural causes of death. The appellate court affirmed the district court's denial of habeas relief, applying the deferential standard for evaluating ineffective assistance of counsel claims. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Purchaser Credit on Timber Sale Contracts (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE · FR-2026-10-07 / 2026-20512

    official summary: The United States Department of Agriculture, Forest Service (Forest Service or Agency) is making purely technical, clarifying amendments to its existing regulations relating to timber purchaser credit in timber sale contracts on National Forest System lands. The authority to use purchaser credit ended in April 1999, and there are no timber contracts subject to this expired authority. This final rule removes sections regulating purchaser credit because these regulations are now obsolete. The removal is necessary to reflect the statutory repeal of purchaser credit authority after April 1, 1999, and the elimination of expired contractual provisions. FR-SEL-01

    Energy Conservation Program: Test Procedures for Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY · FR-2026-10-07 / 2026-20517

    official summary: The Department of Energy (“DOE” or “the Department”) is withdrawing the test procedure for commercial warm air furnaces adopted under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, specifically appendix B, “Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency Two).” Upon reconsideration, DOE has determined that appendix B would have an uncertain increase in representativeness that does not outweigh the likely increase in burden. DOE has also determined that withdrawing the appendix B test procedure would be consistent with the proposed Process Rule, which states that for certain categories of equipment, including CWAFs, DOE will adopt the industry test procedure, as contemplated by EPCA, except in very limited circumstances. Commercial warm air furnaces will continue to be subject to the testing requirements of appendix A, “Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency).” FR-SEL-01

    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY · FR-2026-10-07 / 2026-20520

    official summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a permanent security zone extending 40 yards into the navigable waters of the main channel of Los Angeles Harbor, including the perimeter of the Coast Guard Base on Terminal Island in San Pedro, CA. This is necessary for the security of military service members on board vessels moored at the pier, and military members and government property. All persons and vessels will be prohibited from entering, transiting through, or anchoring within a portion of Los Angeles Harbor's Main Channel surrounding Terminal Island, unless authorized by the Captain of the Port Los Angeles—Long Beach. FR-SEL-01

    Privacy Act of 1974; Implementation (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE · FR-2026-10-07 / 2026-20532

    official summary: In the Notice section of today's Federal Register , the Office of the Pardon Attorney (PARDON), a component within the United States Department of Justice (DOJ or Department), has published a notice of a new system of records, Firearms Rights Restoration Electronic Records Database (FRRERD), JUSTICE/OPA-002. In this notice of proposed rulemaking, PARDON proposes to exempt this system of records from certain provisions of the Privacy Act in order to safeguard confidential information compiled at various stages of the criminal law enforcement process; and compiled for the purpose of ensuring the integrity of the adjudicatory process involving eligibility and suitability determinations concerning the restoration of an applicant's federal firearms rights pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 925(c) and 28 CFR 107.1 et seq. For the reasons provided below, the Department proposes to amend its Privacy Act regulations by establishing an exemption for records in this system from certain provisions of the Privacy Act. Public comment is invited. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: The FAA is revising a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2014-16-22 and AD 2017-25-13, which apply to certain Airbus SAS Model A330-200, A330-200 Freighter, A330-300, A340-200, A340-300, A340-500, and A340-600 series airplanes; and AD 2024-25-11, which applies to certain Airbus SAS Model A330-200, A330-200 Freighter, A330-300, A330-800 and A330-900 series airplanes. The FAA is proposing this airworthiness directive (AD) to address the unsafe condition on these products. Since these actions would impose an additional burden over those in the NPRM, the FAA is requesting comments on this SNPRM. FR-SEL-02
